title: Asking Someone's Age
label: ch:ta-asking-age
canDo: I can ask someone's age in both the casual possessive shape and the formal dative-plus-become shape, and answer with my own.

payoff.summary: Ask "un vayasu enna?" casually, ask "unakku ettanai vayathu aakirathu?" formally, and answer "enakku irupathu vayathu aakirathu."
payoff.note: Below the 0.5 floor by sequence, not by omission: TA-C19-age-register-grammar (680) assesses all three spoken atoms the chapter teaches (vayathu and both register shapes). The other four — the ி sign (TA-SCRIPT-DRIZZLE-09, TA-S09-i-sign, 685), ச and a hand-written சரி (TA-SCRIPT-CA-ONE-LETTER-01, TA-SCRIPT-WRITE-SARI-02, TA-W07-write-sari, 690) and ே (TA-SCRIPT-RECOG-123, TA-S123-vowel-sign-ee, 691) — are taught by script lessons sequenced after it, so the payoff cannot honestly assess them and none of those lessons is a fitting payoff for asking someone's age.
